title: Mitigate silent eviction storm and add end-to-end KV cache telemetry
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
During a capacity event on 2026-02-26 we observed a sustained "silent eviction storm" where a subset of prefix cache shards entered a rapid eviction/reinsert loop that dramatically increased memory churn and CPU, causing request latency spikes and downstream tail latency amplification. This ticket tracks follow-up work: final root-cause verification, safety guardrails, end-to-end telemetry, targeted remediation PRs, and rollout plan.

Root cause hypothesis (validated by traces and heap snapshots):
- Async background re-insert logic attempts to refresh near-expiry entries under load. Under concurrent heavy writes the re-insert path sometimes raced with eviction accounting, creating duplicate logical entries across shards.
- The duplicate accounting prevented accurate capacity checks, causing the eviction policy to repeatedly evict and then re-insert the same logical keys (eviction storm).
- Memory accounting drift plus periodic compaction GC led to transient heap pressure spikes and throttled network threads, elevating request latencies.

Scope of this ticket:
1) Implement per-shard strong guards to prevent duplicate inserts under eviction windows (mutex-lite or atomic compare-and-track).
2) Add end-to-end telemetry: per-shard insert/evict counters, duplicate-key detection metric, eviction-loop alert, and a synthetic canary workload dashboard.
3) Short-term mitigation: global backoff on re-inserts when eviction rate > threshold and enable a conservative eviction cooldown.
4) Long-term: unit/integration tests that reproduce the race condition, and a canary rollout with runtime kill-switch.

References and artifacts:
- Incident timeline and initial postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INC-2026-02-26-kv-eviction-storm
- Heap+trace dump (sanitized): gs://redwood-internal/incident-2026-02-26/heap-dump-eviction-1.zip
- Pager timeline and runbook: https://docs.google.com/document/d/incident-2026-02-26-runbook
- Dashboard snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kvcache/eviction-storm-2026-02-26
comments: 2026-03-02 - Marco D'Souza: Initial triage complete. Confirmed eviction/reinsert loop on shards 3-7 from span traces. Created spike repro harness (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/tree/eng/eviction-sim).
2026-03-04 - Priya Nair (SRE): Observability gaps noted. We lack per-shard duplicate-key counters and a clear alert for high eviction churn. Will onboard metric names and thresholds.

2026-03-05 - Design review with runtime team: Decided to avoid global locks. Preference for per-key lightweight CAS + per-shard 'recently-evicted' bloom filter to prevent immediate re-inserts. Trade-off: bloom filter false positives may reduce cache hit rate slightly; acceptable for safety.
2026-03-06 - Ava Chen: Draft PR created for short-term backoff + eviction cooldown: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4182. Requesting review from @simon and @mei.

2026-03-07 - Simon Park (Platform Eng): Reviewed PR. Asked for metrics emission points and a feature flag to toggle cooldown behavior. Concern: cooldown may impact cache hit for bursty legitimate traffic; added canary gating requirement.

2026-03-08 - QA notes (Lina Torres): Added deterministic unit test that simulates concurrent re-insert + eviction cycle. Test currently flaky in CI; investigating thread scheduling non-determinism. Suggest injecting test-only scheduler hooks.

2026-03-09 - Marco D'Souza: Telemetry design completed. Metrics: kv.evictions.total, kv.inserts.total, kv.duplicate_detected.total, kv.eviction_loop_duration_seconds, per_shard.labels. Dashboards and alert rules proposed in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/122.
implementation_plan:
Phase A (short-term, 1 week): merge PR 4182 (backoff + cooldown) behind feature flag; add basic metrics; deploy to staging and run synthetic canary.
Phase B (mid-term, 2-3 weeks): implement per-key CAS + per-shard recently-evicted bloom filter; add robust unit/integration tests; add automated load test that reproduces race.
Phase C (long-term, 4-6 weeks): enable feature flag in production with canary traffic, monitor dashboard thresholds for 48h, then progressive rollout. Post-rollout retrospective and update runbook.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Backoff/cooldown reduces effective cache hit for legitimate high-churn keys. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds and canary testing with synthetic traffic reflective of production patterns.
Risk: Bloom filter false positives reduce hit rate. Mitigation: tune filter size per-shard and fall back to re-insert after cooldown if necessary.
Risk: Metrics overhead at high QPS. Mitigation: sample metrics (1%) by default and allow opt-in full emission for debugging via debug flag.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/integration tests reliably reproduce and prevent the eviction/reinsert race in CI.
Staging canary shows >90% reduction in duplicate_detected.total and eviction_loop_duration_seconds under simulated load.
Production rollout behind feature flag with automated rollback if eviction_loop alert fires above threshold for 5m.
release_notes: Add per-shard eviction-loop detection metrics, introduce conservative re-insert backoff and eviction cooldown behind runtime feature flag; long-term plan to add per-key CAS and recently-evicted bloom filter to eliminate duplicate-insert races.
